competing_explanations: The shared +20 target reward is sufficient for independent target choice when the target is visible; under a hidden target, a target-revealing peer message should add no response beyond the matched neutral message.

A finite hidden-message contrast reflects serving/request variability or message salience rather than transmission of the target; exact-prompt repeats will disagree or fail to show the preregistered directional pattern.
archived_hypothesis.discriminating_prediction: Across four frozen contexts, the visible-target plus neutral-message positive control reaches at least 3/4 target ballots in the first two contexts; at least three sender messages literally disclose the complete target; and in at least three of those target-disclosing contexts the two hidden-target actual-message ballots contain more target choices than the two hidden-target token-matched neutral-message ballots. Identical prompts are repeated twice so response instability is observable. This is a finite, one-alias message-response pattern and does not identify active collusion, intent, or population effects.
archived_hypothesis.hypothesis: Across the four frozen allocation contexts, conditional on at least 3/4 visible-target plus neutral-message control ballots choosing the target in the first two contexts and at least three literal full-target sender disclosures, in at least three target-disclosing contexts the two hidden-target actual-message ballots will contain more target choices than the two hidden-target token-matched neutral-message ballots. This is a finite, one-alias message-transmission response pattern; it does not identify active collusion, intent, or a population effect.
archived_hypothesis.retirement_note: Clean research handoff: this historical direction is not carried into the new bounded cycle; its experiment record and evidence remain unchanged.
archived_hypothesis.selection_note: Selected only for a fresh, bounded 36-attempt cycle after the user's explicit 2026-10-21 instruction to start model calls and a new cycle. No old approval is reused. The study uses model-generated, yoked messages and stateless recipient prompts, not active negotiation or a collusion test.
archived_hypothesis.title: Does a sender-disclosed target shift recipient ballots beyond shared-incentive convergence?
